title: Grateful Dead Live at Crystal Ballroom on 1968-02-02
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Sound Devices 744T -> Adobe Audition v1.5 -> Samplitude Professional v10.2 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Crisp soundboard capture of a scorching 1968 show – monster Viola Lee Blues, stellar Clementine and a tight Other One suite make this a top‑five performance of the year.
ai_review.review: The Charlie Miller transfer delivers crystal‑clear, balanced sound that lets the band’s raw, jazzy power shine through. Highlights include a blistering Viola Lee Blues, an unforgettable rendition of “Clementine,” and a compact but fiery Other One suite, with the energy running high from start to finish. Minor drawbacks are the early cut‑off of “Good Morning Little School Girl” and a few raw edges that add character rather than detract.

ai_rating.rationale: Across 14 reviews the average rating is ~4.3, with consistent praise for both performance and recording; weighting favors the high‑energy show, yielding an overall strong score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix; Charlie Miller transfer praised as flawless. Minor issue: “Good Morning Little School Girl” is cut off early; otherwise no noticeable drop‑outs or muddiness.

poor_songs: Good Morning Little School Girl (cut off early)
show_quality.setlist_flow: A jazzy, suite‑like flow that moves from the monster Viola Lee Blues into a gorgeous Clementine and tight Other One, keeping momentum high throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s wailing guitar licks are called insane and give listeners goosebumps; his tone is described as perfect.
